prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: D1 (1N4148W-7-F, SOD-123) is mounted with the cathode on the load and the anode on the supply rail. board_04.kicad_pcb: D1 pad '1' (net SW_LOAD) at (5.945, 26.71) and pad '2' (net VCC_5V) at (9.215, 26.71). For a SOD-123 diode KiCad's own reference footprint D_SOD-123 puts pad 1 at x=-1.65 and the cathode band at the pad-1 end, and the 1N4148W symbol in KiCad's Diode.kicad_sym maps pin 1 = K (cathode), pin 2 = A (anode) (inherited from 1N4001_1_1). The board's D1 footprint is an exact pad-for-pad match to that reference (max pad error 0.0000 mm, identity transform), so board pad 1 IS the cathode end. With the cathode on SW_LOAD and the anode on VCC_5V, the diode is FORWARD biased in steady state: VCC_5V anode to SW_LOAD cathode, forward voltage ~0.7 V at 5 V. It does not block the flyback - it conducts it, and it is a 5 V to 0 V short path through the diode whenever the transistor is on.
expected: For a flyback diode across an inductive load the cathode goes to the supply rail and the anode to the switched load node, so the diode is reverse biased in steady state and only conducts while the load's inductance collapses. Here the cathode (D1 pad 1) must be on VCC_5V and the anode (D1 pad 2) on SW_LOAD.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/footprint_orientation_vs_kicad_ref.txt (SOD-123 = EXACT identity match to KiCad Diode_SMD:D_SOD-123, max pad error 0.0000 mm); board_04.kicad_pcb lines 110-123: pad "1" smd rect (at -1.635 0) (net "SW_LOAD"), pad "2" smd rect (at 1.635 0) (net "VCC_5V"); KiCad symbols/Diode.kicad_sym symbol 1N4001_1_1: pin 1 name "K" at x=-3.81, pin 2 name "A" at x=+3.81, and symbol "1N4148W" extends "1N4001" with Footprint Diode_SMD:D_SOD-123

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1's footprint (CircuitOS:DIP-28) is Y-MIRRORED relative to KiCad's reference footprint Package_DIP:DIP-28_W7.62mm. Aligning the two pad sets on their centroids and testing all eight planar transforms, the unique exact match is flipY with max pad error 0.0000 mm (all other transforms 7.62 mm or worse). Consequence: the board's hole labelled 'pad 7' is NOT the ATmega328P VCC pin - the footprint is drawn so that the hole at the pin-1 end is numbered 28. Because a DIP is mounted with its notch (pin 1) at one fixed end, the chip can only go in two ways, and the board's net assignment is wrong in BOTH: (a) chip notch at the board top end (y-min) - the real ATmega328P VCC pin 7 lands in the hole the net-list calls 'pad 8' (GND) and the real GND pin 8 lands in the hole called 'pad 7' (VCC_5V): VCC shorted to GND, i.e. the rail is dead shorted through the chip. Real AVCC pin 20 lands in 'pad 23' (no net) and real PB0 pin 14 lands in 'pad 1' (no net). (b) chip notch at the board bottom end - real VCC pin 7 lands in 'pad 21' (no net), so the chip has NO supply at all; real PB0 pin 14 lands in 'pad 28' (no net) so SW_CTRL is not driven; and the only netted hole, 'pad 14' (SW_CTRL), receives the chip's real pin 28 (PC5), not PB0. In neither orientation does the net named SW_CTRL land on the chip's PB0, and in neither orientation do the chip's two ground pins both reach GND while VCC reaches VCC_5V. The board is unusable in both ways the chip can be fitted. Equivalent statement from the datasheet side: ATmega328P-P pin map is 1=RESET/PC6, 7=VCC, 8=GND, 14=PB0, 20=AVCC, 22=GND, 28=PC5 (resolved from MCU_Microchip_ATmega.kicad_sym ATmega328P-P extends ATmega48PV-10P).
expected: A DIP-28 footprint must be drawn so that pad 1 is the hole at the notch/pin-1 end and the pad numbering increases anticlockwise as seen from the top, matching Package_DIP:DIP-28_W7.62mm. Then the hole carrying VCC_5V is the chip's pin 7, GND holes are pins 8 and 22, and the SW_CTRL hole is pin 14 (PB0), so the part is correct in the only orientation it can be fitted in.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/chip_pin_map.txt (both orientations, max mapping error 0.0000 mm); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/footprint_orientation_vs_kicad_ref.txt (DIP-28: flipY EXACT, max pad error 0.0000 mm; all others >= 7.62 mm); board_04.kicad_pcb lines 279-479 (pad 1 at (at -3.81 16.51), pad 7 at (at -3.81 1.27) net VCC_5V, pad 8 at (at -3.81 -1.27) net GND, pad 14 at (at -3.81 -16.51) net SW_CTRL, pad 20 at (at 3.81 -3.81) net VCC_5V, pad 22 at (at 3.81 1.27) net GND, pad 28 at (at 3.81 16.51)); KiCad footprints/Package_DIP.pretty/DIP-28_W7.62mm.kicad_mod (pad 1 at (0 0), pad 14 at (0 33.02), pad 28 at (7.62 0)); KiCad symbols/MCU_Microchip_ATmega.kicad_sym ATmega328P-P

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: Two GND vias are drilled essentially on top of two U1 through-holes, so the drill files physically merge them and the pad's plated barrel is destroyed. Via at (16.6, 21.52) drill 0.4 mm vs U1 pad 8 hole (16.51, 21.59) drill 0.8 mm: centre distance 0.114 mm, sum of hole radii 0.600 mm, so the two holes overlap by 0.486 mm - a single drill cannot produce them. Via at (24.2, 24.12) drill 0.4 mm vs U1 pad 22 hole (24.13, 24.13) drill 0.8 mm: centre distance 0.071 mm, overlap 0.529 mm. The exported drill file (probe.drl) lists X16.6Y-21.52 on tool T1 (0.400) and X16.51Y-21.59 on tool T2 (0.800) as two separate hits 0.114 mm apart - a 0.4 mm bit cannot make a 0.114 mm offset hole. The board's own DRC under the shipped rules does NOT report this, because board_04.kicad_pro sets min_hole_to_hole = 0.0; re-running DRC with a 0.25 mm hole-to-hole minimum raises the count from 10 to 14 and produces 4 hole_to_hole violations, 2 of which are these pairs.
expected: A plated via must not be placed within (hole radius + pad hole radius) of a component's plated through-hole. The 0.4 mm via needs at least 0.4 + 0.4 = 0.8 mm of centre-to-centre separation from a 0.8 mm PTH, and a typical fab requires >= 0.25 mm of copper/hole separation between distinct holes.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/drc_fab_profile.json (4 hole_to_hole violations, e.g. 'Drilled hole too close to other hole (board setup constraints min 0.2495 mm; actual 0.0000 mm)' for Via [GND] at 16.6,21.52 vs PTH pad 8 [GND] of U1); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/board_04.drl (T1C0.400 hits X16.6Y-21.52; T2C0.800 hit X16.51Y-21.59 - 0.114 mm apart on different bits); board_04.kicad_pcb lines 1049-1080 (the four vias) and 329-336/421-428 (U1 pads 8 and 22); board_04.kicad_pro rules min_hole_to_hole = 0.0

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board's own DRC reports 3 unconnected items (severity=error) on net GND, but the board is shipped with the GND zone UNPOURED: the .kicad_pcb contains a B.Cu zone (net GND) but zero filled_polygon data, and the gerber exported from the delivered file has 0 G36/G37 regions on B.Cu (2155 bytes - pads and vias only, no plane). Consequently the only ground return is the 4 vias and their stubs, and GND is not a closed net on the delivered copper. The 3 DRC unconnected errors are: (1) Via [GND] at 13.6,21.52 vs Track [GND] at 9.325,24.17; (2) Pad 2 [GND] of Q1 (the transistor emitter, 13.61,21.46) vs PTH pad 8 [GND] of U1 (16.51,21.59); (3) PTH pad 22 [GND] of U1 (24.13,24.13) vs Via [GND] at 16.6,21.52. Two further GND vias are reported dangling. Running the same DRC with --refill-zones gives 0 unconnected items, proving the opens are an artefact of shipping an unfilled zone, and also that 4 hole_to_hole violations exist in the shipped copper. The emitter of the switching transistor and the MCU ground are not galvanically connected by the delivered copper.
expected: A board delivered for fabrication must have its ground pour actually filled (or, if unfilled, the fills are regenerated by the fab - which is not a safe assumption, and the DRC the product itself ships is run against the unfilled file). The netlist must close: Q1's emitter, C1's ground pad, U1's two ground pins, and the GND plane must all be one connected net.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The design rules shipped in board_04.kicad_pro have every manufacturing constraint zeroed: min_clearance 0.0, min_track_width 0.0, min_via_diameter 0.0, min_through_hole_diameter 0.0, min_via_annular_width 0.0, min_copper_edge_clearance 0.0, min_hole_clearance 0.0, min_hole_to_hole 0.0. The DRC the product ships therefore checks nothing: it reports 10 violations, of which 6 are 'footprint library not found' and 4 are dangling-via warnings, and no clearance, annular-ring, drill or edge error can ever be raised. Re-running the same board with a conventional profile (0.2 mm clearance, 0.25 mm hole-to-hole, 0.3 mm edge clearance) raises the violation count to 14 and exposes 4 hole_to_hole errors that the shipped rules are structurally incapable of flagging. The board's copper-to-edge and hole-size rules are therefore never checked at any point in the product's own pipeline.
expected: A board emitted for a fab should carry the fab's minimum rules in the project file (non-zero clearance, annular ring, drill, hole-to-hole and copper-to-edge), so the product's own DRC is meaningful and a design that violates the fab profile fails before release rather than at the fab.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: Two of the four GND vias are placed so that their drilled hole breaks out of a surface-mount pad they are meant to connect: via at (13.6, 21.52) with 0.4 mm drill and 0.8 mm pad sits on Q1 pad 2 (the emitter, 0.9 x 1.0 mm pad spanning x 13.160..14.060, y 20.960..21.960) - the drill edge is 0.200 mm inside the pad's copper, i.e. the drill breaks through the pad and lands on the pad's solder-mask aperture; via at (9.8, 24.12) sits on C1 pad 2 (0.6 x 0.65 mm pad spanning x 9.025..9.625) with the drill edge 0.025 mm inside the pad copper. A via drilled through an SMD pad puts a bare hole in the middle of the pad's land: the mask opening is no longer annular, solder wicks and bridges, and the pad's own copper is interrupted. The two remaining vias are not on pads at all, which is why the same board also shows 4 dangling-via warnings - the router dropped the via near a pad but never landed it on the pad.
expected: A stitching via either lands squarely on a pad (so the mask aperture is the via's own annulus, with the pad's copper unbroken) or is placed clear of the pad, connected by a track. A via whose drill falls inside an SMD pad's copper is a manufacturing defect.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The footprint the product uses for the transistor, CircuitOS:SOT-23, is a non-standard pin arrangement that does not match KiCad's reference Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23. Aligning on centroids and testing all planar transforms, the closest is rot90 with a 0.163 mm residual - i.e. it is the reference footprint rotated, but with pad geometry that does not coincide. Concretely, the reference SOT-23 has pad 1 (Base) at (-0.9375, -0.95), pad 2 (Emitter) at (-0.9375, +0.95) and pad 3 (Collector) at (+0.9375, 0), whereas CircuitOS:SOT-23 has pad 1 at (-0.95, +1.10), pad 2 at (+0.95, +1.10) and pad 3 at (0, -1.10) - pins 1 and 2 are on the SAME side of the package and pin 3 sits opposite, which is a different pin layout from the real SOT-23 (MMBT2222A / MMBT2222ALT1G, where the datasheet pinout is 1=Base, 2=Emitter, 3=Collector in the SOT-23 arrangement: 1 and 2 on one side, 3 on the other - but the reference geometry places 1 and 2 on the LEFT side and 3 on the RIGHT). The footprint also uses pads 0.9 x 1.0 mm at a 1.9 mm x 2.2 mm pitch, against the reference's 1.475 x 0.6 mm pads at a 1.875 mm row pitch. The 3D model is therefore not the SOT-23 the silkscreen part number names, and the package is a bespoke drawing rather than a library footprint - which is exactly the condition under which a pin transposition (F-0401's class of error) is invisible to any DRC.
expected: The transistor footprint should be a standard SOT-23 land pattern taken from a library, matching the MMBT2222A datasheet pinout (1=Base, 2=Emitter, 3=Collector) and the real package, so that pin numbering, orientation and paste geometry are all unambiguous.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_04/footprint_orientation_vs_kicad_ref.txt ('SOT-23 vs ref: NO EXACT MATCH (best rot90 err=0.163)' with the pad table ref=-0.94,-0.95 / -0.94,0.95 / 0.94,0.00 against cos=-0.95,1.10 / 0.95,1.10 / 0.00,-1.10); KiCad footprints/Package_TO_SOT_SMD.pretty/SOT-23.kicad_mod pads 1/2/3; KiCad symbols/Transistor_BJT.kicad_sym MMBT2222A -> {1:B, 2:E, 3:C}; board_04.kicad_pcb lines 167-213 (CircuitOS:SOT-23 pads)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request says 'drives a 30 mA inductive load' but no load, coil, or connector for one is present on the board. The only connector is J1 (HEADER-2, 22-27-2021): pad 1 on VCC_5V, pad 2 on SW_LOAD, i.e. a 2-pin header where the load would be plugged. The value field on J1 reads '166.667' and on R1 reads '1210' - these are the raw numeric codes (R1's mpn is RC0402FR-071K21L, a 1.21 kOhm part, so '1210' is the 1.21 kOhm code with the multiplier dropped, and '166.667' is 1 MOhm in the same 'value x 10^n' shorthand). Neither the board nor the Board IR states the load current anywhere, so nothing in the delivered artifact is checked against the 30 mA the request specifies, and there is no part to represent the inductive load itself. The transistor MMBT2222A is a reasonable 30 mA switch and R1 at 1.21 kOhm into a base drive of ~4 mA is in the right region, so this is a shortfall in what the artifact lets a reviewer check rather than a wrong circuit.
expected: Either the board should carry the load/its connector with a stated current rating, or the emitted artifacts should record the 30 mA load so the trace widths, base drive and device ratings can be checked against it. A value field of '1210' and '166.667' is not a readable component value in any BOM or assembly drawing.
evidence: board_04.kicad_pcb lines 125-166 (J1 Value "166.667", MPN 22-27-2021, pad 1 net VCC_5V, pad 2 net SW_LOAD) and lines 214-253 (R1 Value "1210", MPN RC0402FR-071K21L, 1.21 kOhm); board_ir.json component attrs for J1 and R1; net membership computed from the .kicad_pcb: SW_LOAD = {D1.1, J1.2, Q1.3} only

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a 30 mA inductive load through a transistor, with a flyback diode across the load. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board is delivered with no schematic at all: the folder contains board_04.kicad_pcb, board_04.kicad_pro, board_04.kicad_prl, board_ir.json, drc.json and drc_summary.json - there is no .kicad_sch file, and the .kicad_prl references no schematic. kicad-cli pcb drc therefore reports schematic_parity: [] - KiCad had no schematic to compare the board against, so the parity check that would catch a pin-number mismatch between netlist and symbol silently had nothing to run on. The product's 'the board matches what I was told to build' check is therefore untestable from the delivered artifact, and the D1 polarity (F-0401) and U1 pin mapping (F-0402) are exactly the errors a schematic-vs-board comparison would have exposed.
expected: A board delivered for fabrication should come with the schematic it was compiled from, so that the netlist, the symbol pin numbers and the board can be cross-checked by KiCad's schematic-parity DRC and by a human reviewer.
